profile_name: Solved Cold Case — Viral Mix (recommended for NexaTube)
based_on: The chronological base of the somber cold-case profile plus the hook and retention techniques of four competitor videos that reached 270K–1.1M views. No names, places or cases from the originals are kept.

tone_of_voice.notes: Feels like a premium streaming documentary: present-tense immersion in the hook, calm authority in the investigation, controlled emotion at the end.

point_of_view.hook: second person, present tense: the viewer is placed inside the ordinary moment ('You are standing in…', 'It is 2:30 in the morning…')
point_of_view.ending: returns briefly to second person for the lesson and the call-to-action

audience_addressing_style: immersive 'you' in the first 60–90 seconds, then invisible narrator; one channel line after the hook, one at the end; occasional rhetorical question addressed to the viewer at chapter turns

hook_style.type: one of four proven openers, chosen per case
options: A. Archival sound first: 2–3 short lines of a real news anchor or a family member's recorded words, then cut to the narrator.

B. Immersive second person: put the viewer in the place and minute just before everything went wrong, with one repeated motif (an announcement, a phone ringing, a song on the radio) that will return at the end.
C. The object that solved it: open on a small piece of evidence ignored for decades ('A stain on a borrowed boot went unnoticed for 36 years') and promise the story of how it named the killer.

D. Three open-loop questions: summarise the crime in 4 sentences, then ask three precise questions the video will answer ('Who did she meet after…? How did investigators find a man who was never a suspect? And why did they decide to wait?').
always_include: number of years the case stayed cold
a promise that the answer was surprising
hook_style.optional_warning: a single sober viewer-discretion line if the case is disturbing

narrative_structure.type: immersive cold open → who the victim was → chronological night → investigation and dead ends → system failures with numbers → the science → the human hero → the reveal → legal outcome → legacy → circular ending
beats_in_order: 2. Channel line + 'Now, let's go back to that night. But before we go any further, you need to know who [victim] was. Not the case, not the headline, the person.'
3. Victim portrait with specific, humanising details (what they loved, a habit, a quote from family).
4. Era and place snapshot in 3–5 sentences.
5. The last hours, minute by minute.
6. Discovery, first investigation, the wrong suspect(s) and why the obsession with them cost time.
7. System-failure ledger: concrete numbers of missed chances (checks, alerts, calls, months) delivered as a short punchy list.
8. Cold years: anniversaries, family campaigns, retired detectives.
9. Science as a story: how the new technique works, in plain words, and why it finally applied here.
10. The hero: the genealogist, analyst or detective, with hours worked and the moment the branches pointed to one family.
11. The reveal: the confirmation sample (a discarded cup, a cigarette), the match odds, the surprise identity.
12. Interview, arrest, plea or trial; strict legal wording.
13. Legacy: laws changed, other cases solved, what the family said.
14. Ending: return to the opening motif or object, one line on what the victim's life was, one practical lesson for the viewer, sign-off 'No case stays cold forever.'
narrative_structure.chapter_turns: every ~800 words end on a small cliffhanger sentence that pulls into the next part ('And that was exactly what investigators had missed.')

pacing.overall: faster than a classic documentary: a new fact, place or person every 2–3 sentences
pacing.hook: short present-tense sentences, repetition of the motif
pacing.middle: medium sentences with numbers; punchy lists for failures
pacing.climax: one-line paragraphs-in-spirit (very short sentences in sequence)

sentence_style.mix: 60% medium declaratives, 25% short punches of 2–7 words, 15% long descriptive sentences
sentence_style.questions: 3–12 per script: only in the hook (option D) and at chapter turns
sentence_style.repetition: a key phrase or motif repeated 3–4 times across the script
sentence_style.numbers: precise and contrasted ('60 visits, not one look at the backyard')

language_style.register: clear cinematic English, vivid but plain
language_style.sensory_detail: light, weather, sounds and objects of the moment, never gore
language_style.technical_terms: explained with an everyday analogy the first time
language_style.legal_vocabulary: 'charged with', 'investigators say', 'he has not been convicted', 'according to court records'

characters.victim: the heart of the story, always 'the person, not the headline'
characters.family: the voice of time passing; one sibling or parent followed across decades
characters.hero: an ordinary professional or volunteer who noticed what the system missed
characters.system: an antagonist of its own (missed checks, lost evidence, tunnel vision), described with numbers, not insults
characters.suspect: introduced late; ordinary on the surface; no glorification, no nicknames that make him iconic

dialogue.use: documented quotes only: news clips, court testimony, police statements, family interviews

emotional_tone.arc: unease → dread → grief → anger at the system → hope through science and people → justice → bittersweet reflection

common_devices: present-tense second-person immersion in the hook
a sound or object motif that returns at the end
three open-loop questions answered across the video
the 'ignored object' as the hero of the forensic story
ledger of missed chances with exact numbers
'Not the case, not the headline, the person.' humanising turn
cliffhanger sentence at the end of each part
then-and-now contrast (age at the crime vs. age at the arrest; sister aged 12 vs. 60 at the verdict)
circular ending repeating the opening image

call_to_action_style.after_hook: 'Welcome to [CHANNEL NAME]. This case took N years to close. Tell us in the comments where you are watching from, and if you are new, subscribe. It keeps us digging. Now, let's go back to that night.'
call_to_action_style.closing: 'If this case stayed with you, subscribe and share it. And remember, no case stays cold forever.'

visual_cue_prompts.note: Never written in the final script. Use them only for the separate shot list.
visual_cue_prompts.hook: archival news frame in a TV frame, the motif object in close-up, 3D night establishing shot with fog and practical lights, date and place typed on screen
visual_cue_prompts.victim_portrait: real photos with depth parallax, polaroid or case-file frame, name and age lower third
visual_cue_prompts.night_timeline: 3D road or house at night, clock overlays, route on a map
visual_cue_prompts.failures_ledger: big animated numbers, stamped documents, highlighted report lines
visual_cue_prompts.science: animated family tree spreading across a dark board, DNA helix, branches converging on one name
visual_cue_prompts.reveal: the confirmation object in a lit evidence bag, suspect photo young vs. old
visual_cue_prompts.court_and_legacy: courthouse exterior, highlighted charges, list of laws or other solved cases
visual_cue_prompts.ending: same image as the hook, then the victim's photo with name and years

safety_and_compliance: Facts only; mark uncertainty ('investigators believed', 'according to court records').
Anyone not convicted is 'charged' or 'accused', never 'the killer'.
One plain sentence for the cause of death; no gore.
Minors: no sexual detail, no abuse description, no AI recreation; follow the channel rule on whether child-victim cases are covered at all.
Victims only through real photos or anonymous silhouettes; the accused may be shown by mugshot or a labelled AI recreation in non-violent scenes.

script_formatting_rules.parts: The final script must be sectioned into 10 parts, each part at least 800 words.
script_formatting_rules.total_length: The full script must be 8,000+ words in total.
script_formatting_rules.no_headings: No section headings, no part numbers, no titles inside the text.
script_formatting_rules.no_line_breaks: No line breaks: the whole script is one continuous block of text.
script_formatting_rules.no_symbols: No underscores, no bullet points, no brackets, no stage directions, no visual cues, no comments.
script_formatting_rules.no_wrappers: No introductory statement and no closing statement outside the narration itself.
script_formatting_rules.delivery: Send the whole script in one batch, only the script text, with nothing before or after it.
